english.title: Fail to hand over travel documents when required by examining officer

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: anti social behaviour crime and policing act 2014

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed, without reasonable excuse, to hand over all travel documents in your possession, namely **(..SPECIFY TRAVEL DOCUMENTS NOT HANDED OVER..), when required to do so under paragraph

(A)_[2(2)(a)]_
(B)_[3(3)(a)]_

of Schedule 8 to the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 5(1) and (3) of Schedule 8 to the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
fail to hand over travel documents
when required by examining officer

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: 'Examining officer' includes constables, immigration officers and designated general customs officials, see paragraph 1(1) of Schedule 8 to the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. In relation to paragraph 3(3)(a), until 2nd April 2017 the power to require a person to hand over travel documents was only available to constables.
